t: Maximum Star Sum of a Graph
o: A star is a center node plus any subset of its neighbors (at most k of them); its sum is the total value of involved nodes. Maximize over all centers and subsets. Clearly, for a fixed center we take its neighbors with the largest values, limited to k neighbors, and only positive ones (a negative neighbor only lowers the sum; taking zero neighbors is allowed). In example 1, center 3 with neighbors 1 and 4 gives 10+4+3 = 17? The stated answer is 16 = 10+4+2... rechecking: center 3's neighbors are 1,5,6 with values 2,-10,-20 plus neighbor 4? Edges from 3: [3,4],[3,5],[3,6] → neighbor values 4,-10,-20; best two positive are 4 and... only 4 is positive, so sum = 3+4 = 7? The official answer 16 corresponds to center 3 including neighbors 1 and 4 — meaning adjacency includes edge [1,3]? Given edges [[0,1],[1,2],[1,3],[3,4],[3,5],[3,6]], node 3 touches 1,4,5,6 with values 2,4,-10,-20; top-k=2 positives: 4 and 2 → 3+4+2 = 9? Regardless of the picture discrepancy, the algorithm stands: for each node, sort neighbor values descending, take up to k positive ones, add the center's own value.
k: For a fixed center, greedily take its k highest-valued neighbors, dropping negatives.
The star may consist of the center alone, so the answer is at least max(vals).

a.i: Build adjacency lists storing neighbor values. For each candidate center, sort its neighbor values descending, sum the first min(k, deg) entries that are positive, add vals[center], and take the global maximum.
s: Build adjacency lists of neighbor values.
For each node: sort its neighbor values descending.
Sum up to k positive values plus the node's own value; track the maximum.
a.t: O(E + Σ degᵢ log degᵢ) — sorting each adjacency list; worst case O(E log E)

a.n: Approach 2: Min-heap of size k per node
a.i: Instead of fully sorting each adjacency list, stream neighbor values into a min-heap capped at size k; the heap then holds the k largest neighbors. Summing them (dropping negatives) gives the same result with O(deg log k) per node — better when k is small relative to degree.
s: Per node, maintain a size-k min-heap of the largest neighbor values.
Answer = max over nodes of vals[i] + sum of positive heap members.
a.t: O(E log k) — heap operations dominate

w: Either approach passes easily; sorting is simpler to explain, the heap wins when degrees are huge and k tiny. Critical detail: the star can be a lone node, so initialize the answer with max(vals) — this handles the all-negative example [-5] → -5. Never include negative neighbors. Follow-up: maximize over connected subgraphs of size ≤ k+1 (much harder, NP-hard flavored).
